q: do penguins live in the arctic
a: Penguins are flightless seabirds of the family Spheniscidae, found almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere, with the greatest diversity in Antarctica and the sub-Antarctic islands. There are 18 species, ranging from the little blue penguin (about 33 cm tall) to the emperor penguin (up to 1.2 meters and 45 kg). Penguins are highly adapted for swimming and diving — their wings evolved into flippers, they can reach speeds of up to 22 mph in water, and emperor penguins can dive over 500 meters deep. Their dense, waterproof feathers and a thick layer of blubber keep them warm, and they huddle together to survive Antarctic winters. Penguins eat fish, squid, and krill, and they breed in large colonies. Contrary to popular belief, all penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere — none are native to the Arctic, which is home to the similar-looking but unrelated great auks (now extinct).
